items.title: Section: Impermanence's Final Two Aspects — It Will Happen, and It Already Has

items.zh: 依外別離無常性者，謂現前有資生財寶，先未變異，未為別離無常滅壞；後時為王、盜賊、非愛，及共財等之所劫奪，或由惡作加行失壞，或方便求而不能得。
items.en: As for the impermanence of external separation: one presently has requisite wealth, not yet changed, not yet destroyed by the impermanence of separation; but later it is seized by rulers, by thieves, by an enemy, or by a co-owner, or lost through past misdeeds together with present ill-judged undertakings, or, though diligently sought by every means, simply cannot be obtained.

items.zh: 如是等類，應知是名由別離行知無常性。云何復由法性行故觀無常性？
謂即所有變異無常、滅壞無常、別離無常，於現在世猶未合會，於未來世當有法性。如實通達如是諸行，於未來世當有法性。如是等類，名為通達法性無常。云何復由合會行故觀無常性？謂即如是變異無常、滅壞無常、別離無常，於現在世合會現前。如實通達如是諸行，於現在世現前合會。
items.en: As for inherent nature: the very impermanence of change, of destruction, and of separation, though not yet come together in the present, will definitely occur in the future by their inherent nature … as for coming-together: this very impermanence of change, of destruction, and of separation, is already come together and present right now in the present. One correctly penetrates that these processes are, in the present, already come together before one.

items.zh: 如是等類，名為通達合會無常。彼於如是內外諸行五無常性，由五種行，如其所應，作意修習、多修習故，獲得決定。如是由證成道理及修增上故，於無常行得決定已，從此無間趣入苦行。

items.title: Section: Suffering's Own Three Aspects — Bondage, the Undesirable, the Unsettled

items.zh: 作是思惟：如是諸行皆是無常；是無常故，決定應是有生法性；如是諸行既是生法，即有生苦；既有生苦，當知亦有老病死苦、怨憎會苦、愛別離苦、求不得苦。如是且由不可愛行趣入苦行。
items.en: One reflects thus: these processes are all impermanent; being impermanent, they must necessarily possess the nature of arising; being subject to arising, there is thereby the suffering of birth; and given the suffering of birth, one should know there is also the suffering of ageing, sickness, and death, the suffering of meeting the disliked, the suffering of separation from the loved, and the suffering of not obtaining what is sought. Thus, by means of the aspect of the undesirable, one enters into the aspect of suffering.

items.zh: 如是復於有漏、有取、能順樂受一切蘊中，由結縛行趣入苦行。所以者何？
以於愛等結處生愛等結，於貪等縛處生貪等縛。便能招集生老病死愁悲憂苦，一切擾惱純大苦蘊。如是復於有漏、有取、順非苦樂一切蘊中，由不安隱行趣入苦行。所以者何？有漏、有取、順非苦樂一切諸蘊，麁重俱行苦、樂種子之所隨逐，苦苦、壞苦、不解脫故，一切皆是無常滅法。
items.en: Because, wherever craving and its fellow fetters find their basis, craving and its fellows arise, and wherever greed and its fellow bonds find their basis, greed and its fellows arise, one thereby comes to accumulate the suffering of birth, ageing, sickness, death, sorrow, grief, and distress — a whole mass of pure, unrelieved suffering … every aggregate that is contaminated, grasped at, and conducive to neutral feeling goes together with coarseness and is pursued by the seeds of suffering and of pleasure; because it is not freed from the suffering of pain and the suffering of change, all of it is an impermanent, perishing phenomenon.

items.title: Section: Emptiness and No-Self Complete the Truth of Suffering's Ten Aspects

items.zh: 如是行者，於能隨順樂受諸行及樂受中，由結縛行趣入壞苦。於能隨順苦受諸行及苦受中，由不可愛行趣入苦苦。於能隨順不苦不樂受諸行及不苦不樂受中，由不安隱行趣入行苦。如是由結縛行、不可愛行、不安隱行增上力故，於三受中作如是說：諸所有受皆悉是苦。如是名為由無常行作意為[＊]先，趣入苦行。復作是念：我於今者，唯有諸根、唯有境界、唯有從彼所生諸受、唯有其心、唯有假名我我所法、唯有其見、唯有假立，此中可得，除此更無若過若增。如是唯有諸蘊可得。於諸蘊中，無有常恒、堅住、主宰，或說為我，或說有情，或復於此說為生者、老者、病者、及以死者，或復說彼能造諸業、能受種種果及異熟。由是諸行皆悉是空，無有我故。如是名為由無所得行趣入空行。復作是念：所有諸行，與其自相及無常相、苦相相應。彼亦一切從緣生故，不得自在；不自在故，皆非是我。
items.en: Thus, only the aggregates themselves are to be found. Within the aggregates there is nothing permanent, stable, or governing that could be called a self or a being … for this reason, these processes are all empty, since there is no self within them … all these processes are joined with their own particular characteristics, and with the characteristics of impermanence and suffering. Since every one of them arises from conditions, none is self-governing; and being ungoverned, none of them is a self.

items.zh: 如是名為由不自在行入無我行。如是行者，以其十行攝於四行，復以四行了苦諦相。
謂無常行五行所攝。一、變異行，二、滅壞行，三、別離行，四、法性行，五、合會行。苦行三行所攝。一、結縛行，二、不可愛行，三、不安隱行。空行一行所攝。謂無所得行。無我行一行所攝。謂不自在行。彼由十行悟入四行。
items.en: Impermanence is subsumed under five aspects … suffering is subsumed under three aspects … emptiness is subsumed under a single aspect — nothing to be found … no-self is subsumed under a single aspect — powerlessness … through these ten aspects, one thereby enters the four.

items.zh: 復由四行，於苦諦相正覺了已，次復觀察如是苦諦，何因？何集？何起？何緣？由斷彼故，苦亦隨斷。如是即以集諦四行了集諦相。

blocks.text: The ten aspects of suffering, completed.

One's wealth "is seized by rulers, thieves, enemies, or a co-owner, or lost through past misdeeds ripening". The impermanence of change, destruction, and separation "though not yet come together in the present, will definitely occur in the future by its inherent nature"; and when it does come together, that is "coming together".

"These processes are impermanent; being impermanent, they arise; arising, there is the suffering of birth", and of ageing, sickness, death. **Bondage**: "wherever craving and its fellow fetters find their basis, craving arises", and suffering accumulates. **The undesirable**: painful states. **The unsettled**: "every contaminated aggregate conducive to neutral feeling is pursued by the seeds of suffering and pleasure alike".

"Only the aggregates themselves are to be found. Within them there is nothing permanent, stable, or governing that could be called a self." Hence **empty**. "Since every one of them arises from conditions, none is self-governing": hence **non-self**. Venerable Miào Jìng: seeking the self, one finds nothing.
"Impermanence is subsumed under five aspects; suffering under three; emptiness under one (nothing to be found); non-self under one (powerlessness)."

quiz.q: Wealth "lost through 惡作加行" — rendered "lost through some past misdeed now ripening." What do the lectures say?
options: 惡作 is past bad karma, 加行 present unreasonable action; the English drops 加行
quiz.why: "Or lost through some past misdeed now ripening." Master Cháng Bǎi: 加行 is the present condition — unreasonable present methods cause one to lose wealth. Venerable Miào Jìng: you made a mistake in your actions, and so lost your wealth — lost money. The English omits 加行.

quiz.q: "Inherent nature" impermanence "will occur in the future." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: the nature of things — mainly looking to the future
quiz.why: "The very impermanence of change, of destruction, and of separation, though not yet come together in the present, will definitely occur in the future by their inherent nature." Master Cháng Bǎi: 法性 is the nature of things; it mainly looks to the future.

quiz.q: "By the aspect of the undesirable one enters suffering." How many sufferings are listed? The note says eight. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: from birth to not getting what one seeks — seven
quiz.why: "Given the suffering of birth, one should know there is also the suffering of ageing, sickness, and death, the suffering of meeting the disliked, the suffering of separation from the loved, and the suffering of not obtaining what is sought." Venerable Miào Jìng: from birth to not getting what one seeks — seven sufferings. The note's "eight" doesn't match the text.

quiz.q: "Craving and its fetters … greed and its bonds." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish fetters and bonds?
options: the nine fetters are lighter; greed, hatred, delusion are heavy
quiz.why: "Wherever craving and its fellow fetters find their basis, craving and its fellows arise, and wherever greed and its fellow bonds find their basis, greed and its fellows arise." Venerable Miào Jìng: the nine fetters are relatively light; greed, hatred, delusion are heavy.

quiz.q: Even aggregates "conducive to neutral feeling" are unsettled. What of the fourth dhyāna and above, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: though joined with neutral feeling, still unsettled
quiz.why: "Every aggregate that is contaminated, grasped at, and conducive to neutral feeling is pursued by the underlying seeds of suffering and of pleasure alike." Master Cháng Bǎi: even having cultivated up to the fourth dhyāna and above, joined with neutral feeling, it's still unsettled.

quiz.q: "These processes are all empty, since there is no self." How does Master Cháng Bǎi define emptiness?
options: that thing is absent here — no self within the aggregates
quiz.why: "For this reason, these processes are all empty, since there is no self within them." Master Cháng Bǎi: emptiness means that thing is absent here — within these aggregates there's no self; that's called empty.

quiz.q: "Emptiness is subsumed under one aspect — nothing to be found." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: seeking a self and finding none — that's emptiness
quiz.why: "Emptiness is subsumed under a single aspect — nothing to be found." Venerable Miào Jìng: seeking the self, it can't be found — the aspect of nothing to be found; that is called emptiness.
